title: Gross and Microscopic Hematuria (StatPearls)
claims: Microhematuria is defined as 3 or more urinary red blood cells per high-power field on microscopic urinalysis without an apparent cause, while the urine's visual appearance remains normal.
Urinary dipstick findings alone do not provide a definitive diagnosis of microscopic hematuria and require confirmation through one or more microscopic urinalyses.

The absence of microscopic red blood cells in a strongly dipstick-positive sample suggests alternative causes such as myoglobinuria, hemoglobinuria from lysed erythrocytes, or other forms of pseudohematuria.
When hematuria is accompanied by proteinuria, casts, or dysmorphic red blood cells, this usually signals glomerular pathology.
In about 50% of cases a specific cause of hematuria can be identified, meaning no definite etiology is determined about half the time.
High-risk patients require evaluation with CT of the abdomen and pelvis without and with intravenous contrast (CT urogram) plus cystoscopy.
Urine cytology is recommended when carcinoma in situ is suspected or when there is a history of gross hematuria.
The most widely used framework follows the updated 2025 American Urological Association guideline on microhematuria risk stratification.
